answer_text:
Let

\[
f(z)=\frac{1}{(z^2+1)^3}=\frac{1}{(z-i)^3(z+i)^3}.
\]

We integrate \(f\) over the upper semicircular contour consisting of the interval \([-R,R]\) and the semicircle \(\Gamma_R\) of radius \(R\) in the upper half-plane, then let \(R\to\infty\).

The only pole inside the contour is at \(z=i\), and it has order \(3\).

For large \(|z|\),

\[
|f(z)|=\frac{1}{|z^2+1|^3}=O\left(\frac{1}{|z|^6}\right),
\]

so the integral over the semicircle \(\Gamma_R\) vanishes as \(R\to\infty\), since its length is \(O(R)\). Therefore,

\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^3}
=
2\pi i\,\operatorname{Res}(f,i).
\]

Now compute the residue at the third-order pole \(z=i\):

\[
\operatorname{Res}(f,i)
=
\frac{1}{2!}
\lim_{z\to i}
\frac{d^2}{dz^2}\left[(z-i)^3 f(z)\right].
\]

Since

\[
(z-i)^3 f(z)=\frac{1}{(z+i)^3},
\]

we differentiate:

\[
\frac{d}{dz}\left[(z+i)^{-3}\right]=-3(z+i)^{-4},
\]

\[
\frac{d^2}{dz^2}\left[(z+i)^{-3}\right]=12(z+i)^{-5}.
\]

Evaluating at \(z=i\),

\[
\left.\frac{d^2}{dz^2}\left[(z+i)^{-3}\right]\right|_{z=i}
=
12(2i)^{-5}.
\]

Since

\[
(2i)^5=32i,
\]

we get

\[
\operatorname{Res}(f,i)
=
\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{12}{32i}
=
\frac{6}{32i}
=
\frac{3}{16i}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^3}
=
2\pi i\left(\frac{3}{16i}\right)
=
\frac{3\pi}{8}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{3\pi}{8}}
\]
